stances.claim: Contrary to media reports, the SBN did NOT free all sequestered Araneta assets -- only properties 'in the name of' Greggy were cleared, not those 'attributed to him,' because the SBN read its own 2006 resolution literally rather than liberally.

The 2006 SBN resolution should be understood LIBERALLY (covering both 'in name' and 'attributed' assets) rather than LITERALLY, for three reasons: (1) the basis for sequestration was the ill-gotten-wealth assumption, and Greggy's exoneration after PCGG's evidentiary failure dissolves the predicate; (2) the sequestered corporations have no party-standing in Civil Case 0002 to ask for their own release; (3) due process must be accorded to the other shareholders and officers of those corporations who have suffered prejudice.
stances.rhetorical_move: three-reason liberal-construction argument grounded in (a) predicate-failure, (b) party-standing gap, (c) due-process to non-parties

stances.claim: If the PCGG believes the 'attributed' assets should remain sequestered for some independent reason, it must apply for a NEW sequestration order -- the old sequestrations issued because of Greggy's alleged Marcos involvement have been judged 'improvident' and can no longer justify continued PCGG custodianship.

Ill-gotten wealth recovery must be pursued in accordance with the rule of law and due process -- otherwise 'the crusaders for good government would be no different from the raiders of the nation's treasures.'
stances.rhetorical_move: moral-equivalence warning (crusaders becoming raiders if process is ignored)

notable_anecdotes: CJ's correction of media mischaracterization in the opening sentence -- 'Contrary to some media reports, not all the sequestered assets of Gregorio Greggy Araneta III, son-in-law of former president Ferdinand Marcos, have been freed' -- establishing the column's purpose as journalistic clarification before legal analysis.

The list of sequestered companies -- Northern Express Transport, Imexco, Phil. Semi-Conductor Devices, Golden Needle, High Five Philippines -- and the fact that Northern Express had acquired Pantranco North Express properties, showing the post-1987 economic life that PCGG sequestration interrupted for 30+ years.

The civil-code requirement that corporations have at least five owners -- used as the structural reason why non-Greggy shareholders cannot be ignored in the sequestration analysis, since by definition they exist as protected stakeholders.

The closing aphorism: 'the crusaders for good government would be no different from the raiders of the nation's treasures' -- the most compact moral framing in the column, equating procedural shortcuts with the very corruption being investigated.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban corrects media mischaracterization that the Sandiganbayan freed all of Gregorio 'Greggy' Araneta III's sequestered assets: the SBN's Special Fourth Division (Justices Quiroz as ponente, Mendoza-Arcega, and Trespeces) lifted sequestration only over properties 'in the name of' Araneta -- not those 'attributed to him' -- by reading its own 2006 resolution literally rather than liberally. He traces the chronology: the PCGG's July 16, 1987 complaint against Marcos and heirs including Greggy (Marcos son-in-law and Irene's husband) targeting Northern Express Transport, Imexco, Phil. Semi-Conductor Devices, Golden Needle, and High Five Philippines; the SBN's grant of Greggy's demurrer on December 6, 2005; the SC's affirmation in Republic v. Marcos-Manotoc on February 8, 2012; and Greggy's subsequent motion to lift sequestration of all 'attributed' assets, which the SBN literally limited to 'in-name' properties. CJ argues for liberal construction on three grounds: (a) the predicate for sequestration was the ill-gotten-wealth assumption, which collapsed when PCGG failed to present evidence; (b) the sequestered corporations are not parties to Civil Case 0002 and have no standing to ask for their own release despite 30+ years 'under the yoke of PCGG custodianship'; (c) due process must be accorded to the other shareholders and officers of those corporations (the Civil Code requires at least five owners), who have suffered prejudice. He concludes that if PCGG believes the 'attributed' assets should remain sequestered, it must apply for a fresh order -- the old ones are 'improvident' -- and warns that without rule-of-law fidelity, 'the crusaders for good government would be no different from the raiders of the nation's treasures.'
